question: Plaster of Paris is prepared by heating which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plaster of Paris** (POP) is prepared by heating **gypsum**, which is chemically known as **calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO₄·2H₂O)**.
 
• When gypsum is heated to approximately **120°C**, it loses water molecules and transforms into **calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O)**, commonly known as Plaster of Paris.
 
• The chemical reaction involved in this process is:
 
 
• CaSO₄·2H₂O → CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O (heat)
 
 
 
• Plaster of Paris is widely used for **casting, molding, and decorative purposes** due to its ability to set quickly when mixed with water.
 
• Gypsum is a naturally occurring mineral that is abundantly found in areas with sedimentary rock formations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gypsum:**

 
 
• Gypsum is a soft sulfate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO₄·2H₂O).
 
• It is used in the construction industry to make drywall, plasterboards, and cement.
 
• Gypsum is also utilized in agriculture as a soil conditioner and fertilizer.
 
 
 
• **Baking Soda:**
 
 
• Baking soda is chemically known as **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)**.
 
• It is primarily used in cooking as a leavening agent and in cleaning due to its mild abrasive properties.
 
• Baking soda is not related to the production of Plaster of Paris.
 
 
 
• **Slaked Lime:**
 
 
• Slaked lime is chemically known as **calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)**.
 
• It is used in construction, water purification, and as a neutralizer in acidic soils.
 
• Slaked lime has no role in the preparation of Plaster of Paris.
 
 
 
• **Limestone:**
 
 
• Limestone is composed primarily of **calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)**.
 
• It is used in the production of cement, glass, and as a building material.
 
• Limestone is unrelated to the preparation of Plaster of Paris.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Properties of Plaster of Paris:**

 
 
• Plaster of Paris sets quickly when mixed with water and forms a hard mass.
 
• It is lightweight, durable, and easy to mold into various shapes.
 
• Due to its rapid setting time, it is used in **medical applications** like creating orthopedic casts and molds.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• POP is extensively used in **sculpting, decorative ceiling designs, and wall finishes**.
 
• It is also utilized in making molds for ceramics and jewelry.
 
• In construction, it serves as a protective coating for walls and ceilings.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Aspect:**
 
 
• The production of POP involves heating gypsum, which requires energy.
 
• Care must be taken to minimize environmental impacts during its manufacturing process.
